correctness.rationale: For labelled complete bipartite graphs, every vertex sees precisely the opposite shore, so its update factors exactly through the ordered nonempty color supports (225 pairs). The explicit finite support transition is fully enumerated and the 80 nonzero coefficient entries checked. Each nonzero recurrent support forces all vertices to add one mod four, so labelled first-periodic-entry time equals support entry. Surjection counts U_j yield every labelled depth population for all positive shore sizes. The extinction polynomial and balanced seven-term identity follow by exact inclusion-exclusion; the leading 9^n term gives the 9/16 asymptotic. The bundled checker independently simulates 115600 labelled states, verifies 36 weighted cases and the balanced identity through n=30; the mathematical factor-and-lift proof, not finite experimentation, establishes the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The complete recurrent-state classification for all numbers of GH colors was already known in an accessible earlier mathematical record, and the present claim explicitly excludes it. The four-color contribution is the new complete transient-basin/first-entry census, sharp six-step upper bound, and balanced extinction exponent. Direct comparisons with a general-q periodic theorem, a three-color first-entry census, the different four-color cyclic successor-contact update, published-finding corpus records, and older GH primary literature found no implication of these transient data. Unindexed equivalents remain a risk; the 1995 one-dimensional full text has now been materially inspected and is directed at one-dimensional wave/relaxation regimes rather than complete-bipartite finite basin censuses.
residual_risks: General-q recurrent orbit results were already available; only transient-basin and depth data are newly assessed.
Even with inspected 1995 one-dimensional results, a presently unknown equivalent finite-graph basin formula could exist; absent exhaustive global indexing, priority is bounded.
Unindexed equivalent four-state basin tables are not ruled out by semantic search.

value.rationale: The motivating gap is the prevalence, not mere existence, of persistent excitation from disordered initial conditions in a nontrivial infinite family. An all-color theorem only counts recurrent states; the new first-entry coefficients determine exactly how often each attractor is reached and after how many updates. The sharp cutoff six, exact survival polynomial, and the balanced extinction exponent 9/16 quantify a concrete finite-size nucleation threshold and are not routine from periodic-state counts alone. The 225-support reduction is a reusable structural compression of the dynamical basin problem; it is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a known-table recomputation.
